I aim to reply within 24 hours.. ::: :::: ::: ## What this course is {#sec-what-this-is} An introduction to quantitative methods for international relations and European politics, taught with free and open source state of the art tools: R, Quarto, Git and GitHub, all inside Positron. You will learn regression as a way of describing relationships in data, and Bayesian inference as a way of saying how certain you are about them. The whole term runs toward one skill, an eight-step analysis taking you from a research question to an empirical answer with its uncertainty attached. You see that route in session 1, deepen one part of it each week, and run it end to end yourself in the take-home exam. No programming experience and no statistics beyond descriptives are assumed. ## Where to go next {#sec-where-next} - **[Syllabus](syllabus.qmd)** for the full details: objectives, logistics, grading, the exam, the policies, and what each session covers. - **[Schedule](schedule.qmd)** for dates, slides, homework and sample solutions. - **[Installation guide](installation.qmd)** for the software. Work through it **before the first session**, so problems are easy to fix together rather than urgent. - **[Glossary](glossary.qmd)** for the terminology, which arrives quickly in a course like this.
